'''Mohammad Sami''', FASc and FNASc<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Sami,_Prof._Mohammad|title=Fellowship {{!}} Indian Academy of Sciences|website=www.ias.ac.in|language=en|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> (born 5 February 1955) is an Indian theoretical physicist and cosmologist, known for his work on dark energy.<ref name="COPELAND 1753–1935">{{Cite journal|last=COPELAND|first=EDMUND J.|last2=SAMI|first2=M.|last3=TSUJIKAWA|first3=SHINJI|date=2006-11-01|title=DYNAMICS OF DARK ENERGY|journal=International Journal of Modern Physics D|volume=15|issue=11|pages=1753–1935|doi=10.1142/s021827180600942x|issn=0218-2718|arxiv=hep-th/0603057}}</ref> In 2011, his research paper titled, "Dynamics of Dark Energy",<ref name="COPELAND 1753–1935"/> co-authored with [[Edmund Copeland|Edmund J Copeland]] and Shinji Tsujikawa, was included in the Nobel Prize Committee Document.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/delhi/Jamia-facultys-research-paper-included-in-Nobel-Prize-Committee-Document/articleshow/10595510.cms|title=Jamia faculty's research paper included in Nobel Prize Committee Document - Times of India|work=The Times of India|date=2018-09-30}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Sami was selected for the Indo-USSR scholarship in 1972 for higher education while pursuing Bachelor of Science (BSc) in [[Aligarh Muslim University]], Uttar Pradesh, India. He studied at the Department of Theoretical Physics at [[Patrice Lumumba Peoples' Friendship University of Russia|People's Friendship University]], Moscow, Russia. After attaining Master of Science (MSc), he shifted to the [[Moscow State University]] in 1979 and pursued PhD in High Energy Physics under professor V. Ya. Fainberg, a theoretical physicist. The topic was ''“Higgs Boson Production in lepton-lepton and hadron-hadron Collisions”''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ctp-jamia.res.in/people/cv_sami_2015.pdf|title=Prof. M. Sami CV 2015|website=ctp-jamia.res.in|access-date=17 February 2023}}</ref>

==Career==
Sami completed his PhD in 1983 and joined the [[Savitribai Phule Pune University]] (SPPU). In 1985, he joined [[Jamia Millia Islamia]] as a lecturer in physics. In 2002, he was invited to the [[Inter-University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics]] (IUCAA) in Pune as a visiting scientist for a period of three years.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=2011-11-04 |title=Jamia faculty's research paper included in Nobel Prize Committee Document |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/delhi/jamia-facultys-research-paper-included-in-nobel-prize-committee-document/articleshow/10595510.cms |access-date=2023-12-06 |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

In 2006, the Centre for Theoretical Physics (CTP) was established at Jamia Millia Islamia and he was appointed its first director. He engaged in teaching and research for more than three decades. He is a visiting professor at the [[Maulana Azad National Urdu University]], Hyderabad and the [[Zhejiang University of Technology]], China.{{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}

At the IUCAA, he was a member of the governing board. At the [[BRICS]] Association of Gravity, Astrophysics and Cosmology (BRICS-AGAC),<ref>{{Cite web |title=BRICS Association of Gravity Astrophysics and Cosmology |url=http://www.brics-agac.zjut.edu.cn/login.php?cid=26 |access-date=2018-09-30 |website=www.brics-agac.zjut.edu.cn}}</ref> he was one of the vice presidents from India.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.co.in/citations?user=JiRa4LgAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Google Scholar}}</ref> He is the editor of [[International Journal of Modern Physics|International Journal of Modern Physics D]] (IJMPD) and [[List of MDPI academic journals|Galaxies]] (MDPI). He has been selected as a visiting professor of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], President's International fellowship initiative.{{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}

He is a fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India|National Academy of Sciences]] and [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]''.'' He has been a visiting scientist at the [[CERN|European Organization for Nuclear Research]] (CERN) in Geneva, the [[National Tsing Hua University]] in Taiwan, the [[Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe]] at the [[University of Tokyo]] in Japan, the [[L. N. Gumilev Eurasian National University|Eurasian National University]] in Kazakhstan, the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science at the Nagoya University in Japan,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Jamia professor gets one year fellowship to visit Japan - Times of India |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/home/education/news/Jamia-professor-gets-one-year-fellowship-to-visit-Japan/articleshow/17794651.cms |access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> and is a senior associate at the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) in Italy.

He has undertaken various national and international research projects with the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]], government of India.{{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}

In 2011, his research paper on ''<nowiki/>'Dynamics of Dark Energy''', co-authored with [[Edmund Copeland|Edmund J Copeland]] and Shinji Tsujikawa, was published in the [[International Journal of Modern Physics]] and included in the Nobel Prize Committee Document.<ref name=":0" />

Currently, he is a professor at the Center for Cosmology and Science Popularization at the [[Shree Guru Gobind Singh Tricentenary University]] (SGT University) in [[Gurgaon|Gurugram]], India.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Google Scholar |url=https://scholar.google.co.in/citations?user=JiRa4LgAAAAJ&hl=en}}</ref>

==Awards and distinctions==
In 2015, Sami and his team, the Cosmology and Astrophysics Research Group at the Centre for Theoretical Physics in Jamia Millia Islamia, was conferred the Visitor's Award by the [[President of India]] for research conducted in the field of contemporary issues in cosmology and astrophysics. The research group included Sami, Sanjay Jhingan, Anjan Ananda Sen, and Sushant G. Ghosh.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://presidentofindia.gov.in/writereaddata/Portal/awards/booklet.pdf|title = President award}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pranabmukherjee.nic.in/pr050215_01.html|title=Shri Pranab Mukherjee: Former President of India|website=pranabmukherjee.nic.in|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/home/education/news/President-award-for-central-universities/articleshow/46132320.cms|title=President award for central universities|work=The Times of India|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref>

In 2018, [[Padma Vibhushan]] recipient [[Jayant Narlikar|Jayant Vishnu Narlikar]] nominated Sami for Padma Shri in the field of science and technology.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/padma_Recomendor2rev_01032018.pdf|title=SNominations/Recommendations for Padma Awards 2018 received on Padmaawards.gov.in |website=mha.gov.in|access-date=17 February 2023}}</ref>
